# Part V. Distributive Negotiation {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-note .part-overview icon=false}
## Why this part comes here

Negotiation combines decision and persuasion under interdependence. We begin with its mixed-motive nature, then prepare BATNAs and reservation values before using anchors, silence, concessions, and other value-claiming tactics.
:::

## Guiding questions

- Am I trying to win a moment or succeed in the negotiation?
- What will I do if there is no agreement?
- Where is the bargaining zone, and how uncertain is that estimate?
- What does each offer or concession communicate?

## Bridge to the next part

Claiming value is only half the work. Part VI asks whether differences in interests, priorities, beliefs, risk, or time can enlarge what is available to divide.
